title: Pay Per Call for Agencies: Run Client Campaigns
h1: Pay per call for agencies: how to run client campaigns
description: Pay per call for agencies: set up separate client campaigns, routing rules, quality checks and reports. Read the step-by-step guide.
faq: How do agencies run pay per call campaigns for multiple clients?
Give each client its own campaign with its own tracking numbers, routing rules and written definition of a billable call, so one client's traffic and reports never mix with another's.
What routing rules should an agency set for each client?
Set opening hours, daily caps, state rules, blocked numbers and repeat-caller blocks, and decide a fall-back destination for when the client is unavailable.
How do agencies keep pay per call clients and affiliates informed?
Give buyers and affiliates their own portal access and downloadable statements so they can check call records themselves instead of waiting for manual reports.
body:
Pay per call for agencies means running phone-call campaigns for several clients or buyers at once, with each client's calls, rules and reporting kept separate. To do it well you need a tracking number per campaign, routing rules per client, a clear definition of a billable call, and reports each client can read without seeing anyone else's data. This guide walks through how to set that up.

Why agencies approach pay per call differently

An in-house team manages one set of buyers and one set of rules. An agency manages many. Each client may have different opening hours, daily limits, states they serve and ideas about what counts as a good call. If those rules live in spreadsheets and email threads, mistakes follow: a call goes to a closed office, a cap is exceeded, or a client disputes a report that nobody can reconstruct.

The fix is to treat every client as its own campaign with its own written rules, and to make sure the call record is the single source of truth. If you are new to the model itself, start with what pay per call is.

Step 1: Separate campaigns per client

Give each client at least one campaign. Within it, decide the traffic sources (your own channels or partner affiliates), the target country or state, and the tracking numbers each source will use. Keeping campaigns separate means a problem on one client's traffic never muddies another client's numbers. See call tracking features for how numbers and sources are tracked.

Step 2: Write down what a billable call is

Agree in writing, per client, the minimum call duration, how duplicate callers are treated and any other conditions. Our guide to minimum call duration and the one on duplicate calls cover the common options. Agencies that skip this step spend their time on disputes instead of campaigns.

Step 3: Build routing rules for each client

Routing is where client rules become real. For each client consider:

  • Hours: only send calls while their team is open.
  • Daily caps: stop sending when they reach the volume they have agreed to take.
  • State rules: send only calls from the states they serve.
  • Blocked numbers and repeat callers: keep known bad numbers and repeat calls out.
  • Fall-back: decide where a call goes if a client is unavailable.

If a client wants to compete for calls with other buyers, real-time bidding lets buyers be pinged in parallel so the highest bid above your minimum wins. See how real-time call bidding works.

Step 4: Control quality and traffic partners

If partner affiliates supply traffic, rate their calls consistently. A simple grade such as Good, Watch or Poor makes quality conversations factual, and pausing a source that sends too many short calls protects your clients. More detail in quality controls.

Step 5: Give clients and partners their own view

Clients trust numbers they can check themselves. Portals for buyers and affiliates, plus downloadable statements, mean you are not rebuilding reports by hand each month. Agencies that present a branded experience can also use a white-label portal; read white-label call tracking for what to expect. For payout structure, see pay per call affiliate payouts.

How this works in Insight Dial

  • Create a campaign per client with country and state targeting.
  • Set waterfall routing with hours, daily caps, state rules, blocked numbers, repeat-caller blocks and a pre-transfer check.
  • Use the guided setup checklist and the test-call tool before live traffic arrives.
  • Give buyers and affiliates their own portals, set per-affiliate payout rates and download statements.
  • Get alerts in Slack, Discord, Teams or WhatsApp, and send call data on through signed webhooks or the open API.
  • Turn on AI transcription with speaker labels and one-line summaries per account when you want them.

Pricing is pay as you go: a per-minute call rate plus a monthly price per tracking number, drawn from a topped-up balance. Quotes are available on request; see pricing. For vertical-specific setups, visit the industries hub, such as insurance or legal.

Common mistakes agencies make

The first is launching before test calls are placed, so the first real caller finds the routing mistake. The second is mixing several clients' traffic on one number, which makes it impossible to say which source produced which call. The third is leaving caps and hours as verbal agreements. Writing them into the campaign means the platform enforces them, not someone's memory. Finally, many agencies wait until the first dispute to define quality; agree the grades with partners at the start, and review a sample of calls each week so problems show up while they are still small. Our launch checklist covers the pre-go-live checks in more detail.

A short agency checklist

  1. One campaign per client, with written billable-call rules.
  2. Hours, caps and state rules set before traffic starts.
  3. Test calls placed and checked end to end.
  4. Quality grades agreed with partners.
  5. Client and partner access to their own reports.

If you handle recorded calls or consumer contact rules, check your obligations with your own counsel; this article is not legal advice.
